archetype.name: Early Playoff Exit (pitching-carried)
archetype.definition: A Wild Card team whose 88 wins rested on three front-line starters and a few wins of close-game fortune, and whose thin lineup went quiet in a three-game loss at Atlanta.

report.headline: Elite rotation, thin lineup, lucky record: another one-win October in Philadelphia

recap.finish: 88-74, second in the NL East; lost the NL Wild Card Series 1-2 to ATL
recap.body:
This was a different Phillies team from the ones that ran up 95 and 96 wins the last two years. Those clubs outscored opponents by 0.7 and 0.8 runs a game. This one finished at +0.09, about 15 runs over the season (713 scored, 698 allowed). A margin like that usually produces a .500-ish team. The 88 wins came with 5.4 wins of W vs Run Diff on top, fourth-most in the league. The record says contender. The margin says a team that won its close games and lived on its pitching.

The season came in swings. A 12-19 start through April, when they were outscored 132-101, gave way to a 36-19 run across May and June, with June's 153 runs the best offensive month of the year. July fell back to 9-15. August was the high point at 21-7 and +48 runs, likely home to the nine-game winning streak. September undid much of that: 10-14, outscored 105-89, and a closing week against Milwaukee and Tampa Bay in which they scored 0 or 1 run in four of six games. A ten-game losing streak also sits somewhere in the year. The team was very good for stretches and poor for stretches, with little in between.

The constant was the rotation, graded A+. Cristopher Sánchez (6.2 WAR, 2.91 ERA over 207 innings), Jesús Luzardo (5.5 WAR, 2.86, third on the starters tab) and Zack Wheeler (3.00 ERA) were as strong a top three as any staff had. Their FIPs back up the ERAs, so this was not luck. The team ERA still ranked only 11th because the other two starters gave a lot of it back: Aaron Nola at 4.67 and Andrew Painter at 5.40 combined for over 300 innings. The bullpen (B-) had the same split. Jhoan Duran was close to untouchable (1.82 ERA, 1.41 FIP, 33 saves, second among relievers), but José Alvarado (5.86 ERA) and Orion Kerkering (4.97, 12.7% walks) made the middle innings shaky.

The offense is where the drop-off shows. A lineup that ranked 5th to 8th in runs every year from 2022 to 2025 fell to 19th, with a .707 OPS (22nd) in a park that plays slightly to hitters. The A- hitters grade reflects how good the top of the order was. Bryce Harper (135 wRC+), Kyle Schwarber (45 HR, 130 wRC+), Luis Arraez (4.1 WAR) and Bryson Stott (3.8 WAR) all produced. Below them it thinned out. Trea Turner took 700 plate appearances with a .297 OBP and 83 wRC+, and J.T. Realmuto (68 wRC+), Alec Bohm, Brandon Marsh and Justin Crawford all finished between 68 and 90. Fielding also slipped, from +12.3 runs to -2.9.

The Wild Card Series at Atlanta, the team that won the division by six games, played out the regular season in miniature. They scored nine runs in three games. They lost the opener 5-3, took Game 2 by a run, and lost the finale 6-2 after Nola lasted 1 2/3 innings. Schwarber (204 wRC+) and Bohm (187) hit, but Turner and Stott went a combined 3-for-24 with no walks. Duran, the best reliever in the bullpen, allowed three runs in three innings. It is the third straight October with exactly one playoff win.

highlights.title: A genuine three-ace rotation
highlights.body: Sánchez, Luzardo and Wheeler combined for 15.7 WAR, each with an ERA of 3.00 or lower and a FIP to match. Strikeout rates near 30% and low walk rates drove it, which is the sustainable kind of run prevention. This group is why an offense that ranked 19th still reached the postseason.

highlights.title: Duran locked down the ninth
highlights.body: Duran posted a 1.82 ERA with a 1.41 FIP, a 35.6% strikeout rate and a 4.2% walk rate across 33 saves. He ranked second among 389 relievers on the site. A rough three postseason innings don't change what the full season shows.

highlights.title: The lineup's core still hit
highlights.body: Harper (135 wRC+) and Schwarber (130 wRC+, 45 HR) anchored the order. Arraez and Stott added 7.9 WAR between them, much of it on contact and defense. Schwarber carried that form into October with a 204 wRC+ in the Wild Card Series.

lowlights.title: The offense fell out of the top half
lowlights.body: The Phillies scored at a top-8 rate every season from 2022 to 2025. This year they ranked 19th, with an OPS 22nd in the league, in a 104 park. The cause was depth. Turner's 83 wRC+ over 700 plate appearances and Realmuto's 68 were the biggest drains on a bottom of the order with no average bats.

lowlights.title: The record outran the margin
lowlights.body: A +0.09 run differential per game is the profile of roughly a .500 team. The other 5.4 wins came from close games, which rarely repeat. This was a weaker team than 88 wins suggests, and well below the +0.8 margin of a year earlier.

lowlights.title: Soft spots behind the stars
lowlights.body: Nola (4.67 ERA) and Painter (5.40) pitched over 300 innings combined, so the team ERA ranked only 11th despite the top three. In the bullpen, Alvarado and Kerkering walked too many and posted ERAs near 5 and 6. Alvarado's 3.82 FIP suggests some bad luck, while Kerkering's 12.7% walk rate is a real problem.

arc.note: A 12-19 start through April turned into a 36-19 May and June. The team then sagged in July, surged 21-7 in August and faded 10-14 in September. Streaks of nine wins and ten losses fit that pattern.

recap.nextYear: The part most likely to carry over is the top of the rotation. Sánchez, Luzardo and Wheeler earned their ERAs with strikeouts and few walks, and Duran's season was just as well-supported. The work needed is in the lineup. Behind Harper, Schwarber, Arraez and Stott, five regulars finished between 68 and 90 wRC+, and the offense fell from 8th to 19th in a single year. Fielding also slid back below average. The back of the rotation and the middle relief need upgrades or rebounds, with Alvarado's FIP offering more hope than Kerkering's walk rate. The record also flatters the team. A +15 run differential plus 5.4 wins of close-game luck is the base to start from, not the 88 wins. Without more offense, the true talent level is closer to the low 80s than to the 95-win teams of 2024 and 2025.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; the postseason read rests on only three games.
